status_summary: The administration went further than the recommendation. Executive Order 14256 (2025-04-02) ended duty-free de minimis treatment for goods from China effective 2025-05-02, and later April 2025 orders raised the duties on those low-value shipments. Executive Order 14324 (signed 2025-07-30, 90 FR 37775) suspended duty-free de minimis treatment for all countries, effective 2025-08-29 according to later Federal Register documents. Executive Order 14388 (2026-02-20) kept the suspension in force after the Supreme Court ruling on IEEPA tariffs, citing IEEPA and other authorities, and Executive Order 14389 states that the suspension is unaffected by its ending of IEEPA duties. On 2026-06-24 CBP published interim final rules implementing an indefinite suspension of the de minimis exemption for all modes, including mail. Public Law 119-21 (Section 70531) modifies the statutory de minimis privilege; a secondary source reports the statutory exemption ends 2027-07-01.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14266 raises duties on low-value shipments from China (ad valorem rate from 90 to 120 percent and per-item fee from $75 to $100 on 2025-05-02, then $200 on 2025-06-01), part of the closure of de minimis treatment for China.
Public Law 119-21 enacted; its table of contents lists Section 70531 on modifications to the de minimis entry privilege for commercial shipments.
Executive Order 14324, Suspending Duty-Free De Minimis Treatment for All Countries, is signed (2025-07-30); the suspension takes effect 2025-08-29 at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time.
Executive Order 14388 amends Executive Order 14324 to keep the suspension for all countries, effective 2026-02-24, with postal duties collected at the Section 122 surcharge rate.
Supreme Court holds IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; Executive Order 14389 states the de minimis suspension order is not affected by its ending of IEEPA duties.

The Court of International Trade grants summary judgment to the government in Axle of Dearborn v. Department of Commerce (Slip Op. 26-94), upholding the presidential suspension of duty-free de minimis treatment.

CBP proposes a rule on low-value shipments (91 FR 64532; comments due 2026-12-07) requiring informal entries of goods valued at 2,500 dollars or less to be filed electronically at or before importation, creating an informal mail entry type with tracking-number data, requiring a licensed broker for some consignees and an entry bond, and allowing blanket formal-entry requirements. It cites Executive Orders 14324 and 14388 on the de minimis suspension and states that the 2025 reconciliation law ends the de minimis exemption effective 2027-07-01.

title: End the de minimis exemption that lets low-value Chinese shipments avoid tariffs
uncertainties: The 2027-07-01 statutory end date is reported by Alvarez & Marsal and Wikipedia and stated in CBP's 2026-10-08 proposed rule, but the text of Section 70531 was not read. The 2025-08-29 start of the global suspension rests on Federal Register records and secondary sources. The initial China-only order (Executive Order 14256) was not read; its details are inferred from Executive Order 14266. Whether the Court of International Trade ruling has been appealed was not found.
